## Why benchmarks matter — and where they mislead

- **OmniDocBench has been declared saturated** by LlamaIndex's own blog (mid-2026). Top scores cluster within ~1pp.
- Saturation is real and predictable. Use benchmarks as **filters** (eliminate the worst), not **rankings** (pick the best).
- Vendor-published benchmarks (ParseBench, RD-TableBench) are useful but biased. Cross-validate.
- Your golden set is the only benchmark whose score actually predicts your production behavior (Chapter 11).

## The 2026 benchmark catalog

### ParseBench (LlamaIndex)

- ~2,000 human-verified pages, 167k+ test rules.
- Axes: tables, charts, content fidelity, formatting, **visual grounding**.
- Top: **LlamaParse Agentic at 84.9%**, ~$0.012/page.
- Live leaderboard at parsebench.ai.
- Caveat: published by LlamaIndex. Rule selection inevitably shapes results.

### OCRBench v2

- 10,000+ QA pairs, bilingual (EN + ZH).
- Less useful when production contract is structured extraction (vs. visual text reasoning).
- Worth tracking if your workload has heavy Chinese-language content.

### olmOCR-Bench (AllenAI)

- 7,000+ test cases across 1,400 documents. Unit-test style.
- English-only. Annotations from closed-source VLMs.
- Top open-source: **Chandra at 83.1, OlmOCR-2 at 82.3, dots.ocr at 79.1**.
- Useful precisely because it's English-only and reproducible — great for regression-testing English-heavy pipelines.

### OmniDocBench v1.7

- 1,651 pages + a new 296-page hard subset (April 2026).
- 10 document types, 5 layout types, 5 languages.
- Skills-based evaluation added in v1.7.
- **Considered saturated** — top scores cluster within ~1pp.
- Hard subset is where the discriminating signal now lives.

### RD-TableBench (Reducto)

- 1,000 adversarial tables. PhD-annotated.
- Needleman-Wunsch alignment for table-cell matching.
- Top: **Reducto at ~0.90 similarity**, ~20pp ahead of hyperscalers.
- Vendor-published. Treat as one signal.

### DABstep (Adyen + Hugging Face)

- 450+ real-world data-analysis tasks from Adyen's operational workloads.
- Mixes structured (CSV/JSON) and unstructured (text, manuals) data.
- **Top score: ~14.55% on hard tasks (o4-mini reasoning).**
- The most important 2026 benchmark — for what it reveals about the gap between "extracts correctly" and "answers correctly downstream."
- This is the benchmark that embarrasses the field. Read it whenever you want a reality check.

### SCORE-Bench (Unstructured.io) — new in 2026

- 1,000+ page enterprise dataset: scanned invoices, nested tables, handwriting, schematics, patents, marketing collateral.
- SCORE = Structural and Content Robust Evaluation. Designed for **generative** parsing systems — separates representation diversity from actual extraction errors.
- Worth watching as it matures. Already compares Reducto, LlamaParse, Docling, Snowflake, Databricks, NVIDIA.

### OfficeQA (Databricks) — new in 2026

- Enterprise document-workflow reasoning tasks.
- Frontier agents score **below 50%**.
- Insertion of upstream `ai_parse_document` produces **16% average gain** — the cleanest evidence for the shift-left thesis.
- arXiv 2603.08655 for full details.

## What each benchmark actually measures

*(Render from `data/benchmarks.csv` in Phase C. Add a column for "what it misses" — the underspecified axis for each benchmark.)*

## What benchmarks miss

- **Latency** — most benchmarks score accuracy and ignore wall-clock time. Production cares.
- **Cost-per-correct-output** — benchmarks report accuracy *or* cost separately, rarely jointly.
- **Long-form reasoning** — DABstep is the only one that really tests this, and the ceiling is shockingly low.
- **HITL acceptance rate** — no public benchmark measures the metric that matters most in production.
- **Domain shift** — every benchmark has a distribution. Your distribution is different.

## When to ignore the leaderboard

- When the top 5 cluster within 1–2pp on a metric your team doesn't directly care about.
- When the benchmark is published by the vendor whose model leads it.
- When the benchmark hasn't been updated in 12+ months.
- When your golden set says something different. **Your golden set wins.**

## Named takes

> *"OmniDocBench told us a year ago what works. It can't tell us anymore. If you're still picking vendors by their OmniDocBench number in late 2026, you're not paying attention."*

> *"DABstep is the only benchmark whose top score embarrasses the field. It is therefore the benchmark to watch."*
